headline: CENTCOM says 'vast majority' of Iranian attacks on Hormuz vessels 'unsuccessful'
dek: CENTCOM asserts Iranian attacks on Hormuz shipping are overwhelmingly ineffective: 97% of vessels transiting the strait were not hit; US-coordinated protection covers thousands of ships; Iran's stated objective of closing the strait is failing.
sources: US Central Command spokesman Tim Hawkins to Fox News, via Al Jazeera liveblog: '97 percent of vessels that attempted to sail through the Strait of Hormuz have done so successfully without being hit by an Iranian projecti
fault_line: Is the Hormuz blockade REAL (IRGC mine claims, 'closed' warnings, tanker fires on video) or BROKEN (97% transit success under US escort)?

sections.what_happened: CENTCOM asserts Iranian attacks on Hormuz shipping are overwhelmingly ineffective: 97% of vessels transiting the strait were not hit; US-coordinated protection covers thousands of ships; Iran's stated objective of closing the strait is failing.
sections.what_verified: Gulf News liveblog (Oct 16/17) carries CENTCOM fact sheet: 400 commercial vessels through Hormuz in past week; 50,000+ US personnel deployed across the region; UKMTO reported 12 incidents in a week (10 Hormuz, 1 Gulf, 1 Gulf of Oman) — incident counts corroborate attacks are happening
sections.what_disputed: Iranian sources (Times Now, citing Iran warnings, Oct 17 21:48 IST): Iran warns Hormuz 'remains closed'; IRGC Navy claims second supertanker struck by naval mine Saturday morning (already recorded, 2200-01). IRGC publishes video of tanker fires (Independent Persian). Two narratives cannot both be true — the strait is either open-with-escort (US) or closed/mined (Iran). UKMTO data shows attacks are real; 'successfully transited' counts depend on US-escort coordination numbers.
sections.why_matters: Two militaries, two incompatible Hormuz stories. Iran shows burning tankers; America cites 97% safe transit. The gap between the stories is where the war's economic battle is being fought. Map the incidents (UKMTO) against the claims; end on the pocketbook: $110 Brent while both sides claim victory.
sections.context: Background: Hormuz — UPDATE (extends 2200-01/2300-03): CENTCOM says 'vast majority' of Iranian attacks on Hormuz vessels 'unsuccessful'; 97% of transiting vessels unhit

totw_analysis: Our read: Two militaries, two incompatible Hormuz stories. Iran shows burning tankers; America cites 97% safe transit. The gap between the stories is where the war's economic battle is being fought. Map the incidents (UKMTO) against the claims; end on the pocketbook: $110 Brent while both sides claim victory. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is the Hormuz blockade REAL (IRGC mine claims, 'closed' warnings, tanker fires on video) or BROKEN (97% transit success under US escort)?
